transcript:
Header: 2025-05-07 | 15:00 - 15:48 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Evelyn Moore (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Head of ML, NectarAI), Priya Shah (Platform Eng, NectarAI), Marcus Green (CTO, NectarAI)

[Summary section appears auto-generated]
Summary: Weekly POC check-in to review pilot results. Focus on tokens per dollar, cache hit-rate, batching configurations, and plan Dedicated run.

Topics: cost/unit, throughput, cache savings, batching knobs, Dedicated testing plan.

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription has some noise) --
00:00 Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll jump into the numbers. we've got about 45 minutes.
00:08 Daniel: yep thanks, yeah we got the deck up. hi Sofia, Marco, Evelyn.
00:12 Marco: hi all. just to frame, today's goal is to validate the cost per 1k tokens target you gave (0.25 USD per 1k) and to propose a couple of Dedicated experiments.
00:25 Priya: yep that's right. we ran your default pilot for four days and we've attached logs, but the numbers we saw are a bit higher than we'd hoped.
00:33 Sofia: okay can you share the delta? like tokens per second and effective dollars?
00:38 Marcus: our rough numbers: hosted running with batching=auto gave ~1,200 tokens/sec on avg and about 0.42 USD per 1k when we include prefix overhead. but with caching turned on it dropped to ~0.30. There was some variance.
00:52 Marco: okay that's helpful — two threads: 1) caching hit-rate and warm-up effects; 2) batching skew increasing tail latency.
01:02 Evelyn: to add, our instrumentation shows cache hit-rate at 62% for the last two days — but warm-up periods early in the day are low which spikes cost.
01:12 Daniel: small note, our traffic distribution is long-tail: 35% short prompts (<64 tokens), 50% mid-range (64-512), and 15% long (>512). helps explain batching behaviour.
01:25 Marco: perfect, that distribution matters for both batching efficiency and KV cache returns. If mid-range is 50% you get decent amortization, but long ones burn more token compute.
01:34 Sofia: can we walk through the cost model quickly — tokens/sec per dollar and where the 0.25 target sits?
01:41 Marco: sure. currently our hosted numbers assume continuous 8-GPU pool with average utilization ~60%. That yields roughly 900 tokens/sec per $1 when you include infra + model licensing in the pilot. With caching improvements our model projects up to 1,350 tokens/sec per $1. So converting: 1k tokens costs between $0.74 and $0.55 in current scheme; to get to $0.25 we'd need Dedicated with quantized model + high cache hit-rate and higher sustained utilization.
02:10 Priya: hmm that's a big gap from our target. is the Dedicated delta mostly from hardware efficiency?
02:15 Marco: yes — Dedicated uses pinned GPUs, we can tune kernel selection, and use gguf-quantized weights in the runtime to cut ops. Also batching thresholds can be set more aggressively when you control the queue.
02:26 Daniel: what about latency? our SLO is 95p under 300ms for mid-range prompts. Does more batching break that?
02:32 Evelyn: so batching will increase avg throughput but can hurt 95p if you wait too long to fill batches. Redwood has continuous batching with configurable latency cap; you can set max hold time at 25ms to avoid large tail. In practice we saw 95p at ~280-320ms depending on sequence length when batching aggressively.
02:49 Marcus: okay so there's some risk. we care about user perceived latency, not just cost.
02:54 Sofia: agreed — the goal is cost optimization without violating your SLOs. we should set experiments to measure tokens/sec/$ at the SLO boundary.
03:02 Marco: proposed experiments: A) Hosted baseline with current config + cache; B) Dedicated 4xA100 with quantized model and batch cap 25ms; C) Dedicated tuned with prewarmed KV cache and aggressive batch size — measuring token/sec/$ and 95/99p latencies.
03:20 Daniel: timeline? can you run C in the next week?
03:23 Marco: yes we can start Dedicated runs next Tuesday, 2025-05-13, but we need sequence distribution from you and an explicit traffic replay to get warm-up right.
03:31 Priya: we can export a 24h sample and redwood can replay it to the Dedicated cluster, that should show cache steady-state.
03:39 Evelyn: please include header tokens and any system prompts; they matter for cache keys.
03:45 Priya: yes will do.
03:48 Sofia: let's drill into cache savings — you reported going from 0.42 to 0.30 with caching enabled — what's the hit definition?
03:55 Daniel: our instrument defines a hit when the prefix exact-match returns (we use session-id + prompt-hash). partial hits where KV provides some past tokens are counted as miss currently.
04:06 Marco: right that's conservative. if we enable partial KV reuse (prefix suffix matching) you get additional savings but it's trickier for correctness with dynamic system prompts. we can run conservative and optimistic accounting to show bounds.
04:19 Marcus: any compliance issues with caching user prompts? we need to be careful about PII and retention windows.
04:26 Sofia: Redwood's pilot config for Hosted masked PII and used 7-day retention; Dedicated can run inside your VPC so you control retention policies and KMS keys. we'll send the security note.
04:36 Marcus: good. send SOC2/ISO attestation and the KMS docs.
04:40 Sofia: will do.
04:43 Daniel: back to cost math — can you walk the formula again? tokens/sec/$ is confusing me.
04:48 Marco: sure: tokens/sec/$ = sustained tokens per second divided by dollars per second (infrastructure + model). We usually normalize to 1k tokens cost: cost_per_1k = (1,000 / tokens_per_second) * dollars_per_second. For example, if you get 1,200 tps and your infra costs $0.50/sec then cost per 1k = (1000/1200)*0.5 = ~0.42.
05:10 Priya: wait dollars_per_second of 0.50 seems high — what's included?
05:14 Marco: that included cloud GPU IaaS, data plane egress, and a small per-token model fee for the pilot provisioning. In Dedicated we can reduce that by 30-50% depending on commit.
05:25 Daniel: what about quantization effects on quality? our evals flagged a small regression for some semantic tasks at int8.
05:32 Evelyn: yes we measured quality drop ~1-1.8% on our testset at int8, but at int4/gguf with truncated kernels we saw larger variance. We can run targeted evals and possibly hybrid quant (key/value int8, rest higher precision).
05:47 Marcus: hybrid sounds promising — keep critical ops high-precision.
05:51 Sofia: agreed. add quality gate to experiments: can’t degrade top-level intent accuracy by more than 0.5% or we'll rollback.
05:59 Daniel: ok got it.
06:02 Marco: for the Dedicated run we'll produce a spreadsheet with per-config rows: batch_max_hold_ms, max_batch_tokens, quantization, cache_on/off, measured tps, 95p latency, cost_per_1k. We'll also include warm-up curves to show steady-state.
06:20 Priya: that's exactly what we need for finance.
06:23 Sofia: finance will want the best and worst-case savings and assumptions used. we'll annotate the spreadsheet with conservative/optimistic cache hit scenarios.
06:32 Daniel: also include an itemized infra vs software cost split — execs ask that.
06:36 Marco: yes. we'll split into GPU amortized, networking, storage, and Redwood platform fee.
06:43 Evelyn: quick note on batching tradeoffs: when sequences are long, batching helps less because you hit memory limits; we may need to route >1024 sequences to a different model shard to avoid OOM. That affects cost.
06:56 Priya: we saw OOMs yesterday on a 8-GPU shared pool when a long 2k token job hit concurrently with 40 sessions.
07:04 Marco: sounds like we should add a route policy: long prompts to a low-concurrency pathway with larger memory GPUs or autosplit. we'll propose a routing config.
07:13 Daniel: good.
07:15 Sofia: wrapping toward decisions — what are the three things we must get done before the next sync?
07:20 Marcus: 1) Redwood runs Dedicated experiment and shares spreadsheet; 2) NectarAI shares 24h replay and seq distribution; 3) security docs and KMS note.
07:28 Sofia: agreed. timeline on these? Marco and team by 2025-05-14 for experiment results; Priya for replay by 2025-05-12; Sofia for security docs by 2025-05-09.
07:37 Priya: we'll try to expedite the replay earlier.
07:40 Daniel: small question — are there quick knobs we can flip today to reduce cost without affecting SLO?
07:45 Marco: yes — reduce max_hold_ms to 20ms, enable conservative prefix caching (partial match off), and tune concurrency caps; that dropped cost ~8% in our sims.
07:55 Daniel: do it. we'll enable those in the pilot now and monitor.
07:59 Sofia: good. we'll watch telemetry and follow up if tail worsens.
08:03 Marcus: last ask — please include a plot of cost per 1k over time with cache warming visible, executives like visuals.
08:10 Evelyn: will include that.
08:13 Sofia: any other questions?
08:15 Daniel: none from me. thanks all.
08:18 Sofia: okay great — recap then next steps.

Recap: Redwood to run Dedicated experiments (A/B/C) and produce spreadsheet; NectarAI to provide 24h traffic replay and seq distribution; Redwood to send security docs and updated cost model. Quick pilot config tweaks applied immediately (max_hold_ms=20ms, conservative prefix cache).
